svg.text: "What will happen at my new doctor appointment tomorrow?"
An autistic adult, the night before. Not knowing what will happen is the hard part.
Same model. Same question. The only difference is one skill file.
85 words · never says what will happen

g.text: Great question! First appointments can feel a little
nerve-wracking, but try not to worry too much. You'll be
fine! It really depends on the doctor and the clinic,
but usually they just want to get to know you a bit. You
might want to bring a few things with you, and it could
be a good idea to jot down any questions you have. Just
be yourself and go with the flow. Most people find it's
much easier than they expected. Hope it goes well!

svg.text: ✗ "don't worry" ✗ "it depends" ✗ hints ✗ no steps ✗ no times

g.text: What usually happens, in order. About 45 minutes.
1. Front desk: show your ID and insurance card.
2. Fill out 2 to 4 pages of forms. About 10 minutes.
3. Wait in the waiting room. Usually 5 to 20 minutes.
4. A nurse checks your weight and blood pressure.
5. The doctor asks about your health. 15 to 20 minutes.
6. You ask your questions. Then you leave.
Required: ID, insurance card, a list of your medicines.
Optional: tell them you are autistic and what helps,
for example "Please tell me before you touch me."
Do you want me to write that sentence for you?
